abstract: We introduce two multiple qubit controlled-unitary gates with different working principles. We employ these gates and existing quantum gates to propose simple and efficient algorithms that generate multi-term orthonormal entangled Bell-like bases. All algorithms thus far known for constructing entangled bases turn out to be special cases of our method. The Bell-like states in any basis is superposition of $2^{m}$-terms with equal probabilities (that is, their amplitudes being $\pm 1/\sqrt{2^{m}}$). The orthogonality of the basis does not permit arbitrary amplitudes. The quantum correlations of these bases are investigated; we find that the Bell-like bases obtained using different controlled-unitaries have different entanglement contents. We also learn that monogamy score is able to distinguish these bases in the situations where other quantum correlations fail to do so indicating that monogamy score is a more fundamental quantum correlation measure. Our approach can be extended to qudit systems as well.

specification.problem: Construct orthonormal bases of multi-term entangled Bell-like states, each a superposition of 2^m terms with amplitudes ±1/sqrt(2^m), using two multiple-qubit controlled-unitary gates together with existing quantum gates, and compare the quantum correlations (entanglement, monogamy score) of bases obtained from different controlled-unitaries.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction. The explicit gate definitions and circuits are not given in the abstract. Only the amplitude structure and orthonormality constraint are fixed. A small finite instance (for example m=1 or m=2) may be assumed later for illustration.

registers.name: control
registers.role: Qubits put in uniform superposition by Hadamards; they control the unitary gates

registers.name: target
registers.role: Qubits acted on by the multiple-qubit controlled-unitary; they carry the entangled Bell-like state

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state |i>, assumed to label the basis element (label bits set by X gates)

steps.description: Apply Hadamard gates to the control qubits to create a uniform superposition of 2^m terms, with signs depending on the label bits.

Apply one of the two multiple-qubit controlled-unitary gates (the details are not given in the abstract) with the control qubits acting on the targets, which entangles them and spreads the terms over target basis states.
Repeat for all initial labels i to obtain the full set of states. The result should satisfy orthonormality, which holds because the circuit is unitary and the inputs are orthonormal.

specification.measurement: Assumed: to identify which basis element was produced, invert the circuit (the controlled-unitary, then the Hadamards) and measure all qubits in the computational basis, which returns the label i. For the correlation study, the entanglement and monogamy score are computed from the state or reduced density matrices, which would need tomography on an experiment.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Read the measured bitstring as the basis label. For the correlation analysis, compute the chosen entanglement measures and the monogamy score from the known state vectors or reconstructed density matrices, then compare the bases obtained from the different controlled-unitaries. The abstract does not define these measures.
